title: Robot Stork Catapult Trajectory Lab
description: A robot operates a spring-loaded catapult to launch a stork across a canyon. The user adjusts launch angle, spring constant, compression distance, wind resistance, and gravity multiplier, then fires and observes the stork's parabolic trajectory with real-time physics. The goal is to land the stork on a floating target platform by tuning all parameters within 10 attempts.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap with es-module-shims) implementing a physics catapult simulation. Load robot.glb and stork.glb from shared_assets/ using GLTFLoader. Scene setup: a ground plane textured as rocky terrain, a canyon gap (dark void) roughly 20-40 units wide depending on parameters, and a floating circular target platform on the far side with a glowing ring. Place the robot on the near cliff edge standing behind a visible catapult arm (a simple box geometry pivoting on a hinge). Seat the stork on the catapult cup. Camera: OrbitControls, initial perspective view from the side showing the full trajectory arc. Lighting: hemisphere light plus directional light with shadows enabled. GUI panel (use lil-gui) with these parameters: launch angle (15-75 degrees, default 45), spring constant k (50-500 N/m, default 200), compression distance (0.5-3.0 m, default 1.5), wind resistance coefficient (0.0-0.5, default 0.1), and gravity multiplier (0.5-2.0, default 1.0). Validate all inputs stay within ranges. A 'FIRE' button triggers the launch: animate the catapult arm rotating up, release the stork, then simulate projectile motion each frame using Euler integration: apply gravitational force (9.81 * gravMultiplier), quadratic air drag (0.5 * windCoeff * v^2 opposing velocity), and initial velocity from spring energy (0.5*k*x^2 = 0.5*m*v0^2). The stork should rotate to face its velocity vector during flight. Draw a trailing dotted line showing the trajectory path. On landing (y <= platform height near platform x/z), check if within target radius: show green particle burst for success or red splash for miss. Display an attempts counter (max 10) and distance-from-target readout. The robot should play a celebratory animation (bobbing up and down) on success. Reset stork to catapult after each attempt. Add a real-time HUD showing current velocity, height, and flight time during trajectory.
